author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Latvian airline airBaltic has filed for voluntary Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in New York as higher fuel costs and an aviation downturn put pressure on its balance sheet, Reuters reported Monday.

The carrier has a $405 million financing commitment from lenders, subject to court approval. The proposed financing carries an interest rate of about 12%, giving the airline cash to operate while it restructures its debts and contracts.

AirBaltic said scheduled flights are expected to continue during the process, which the company hopes to complete by June next year. The airline has about 3,000 employees and operates a fleet of roughly 50 Airbus A220-300 aircraft.

Reuters reported that the carrier has about $583 million in debt and €106 million in taxes and fees. Latvia’s government remains the majority owner, while Lufthansa holds a minority stake; airBaltic is also seeking a strategic investor.
The report remains subject to further verified updates as officials continue reviewing the circumstances.
dek: Latvian carrier airBaltic has entered Chapter 11 restructuring in New York and secured a proposed $405 million financing package to keep flying during the process.
headline: AirBaltic files for Chapter 11 as higher fuel costs strain airline
